title: Return Fraud Inspection Theater
oneLiner: Small ecommerce teams stage suspicious returns, box photos, customer history, and refund rules into a fast approve-deny performance.
theme: 자산 방어 / 역전 - merchant loss prevention with a shareable case-stage metaphor.

phaseA.label: Fun / Portfolio / Experimental
phaseA.targetUser: Small ecommerce sellers, boutique retail ops teams, and returns coordinators dealing with wardrobing, empty boxes, swapped items, and serial refund abuse.
phaseA.keyUx: Operator opens a suspicious return case, reviews unboxing evidence and customer history, runs policy tests, and chooses approve, partial refund, deny, or manual escalation.
requiredUiSections: Suspicious return stage with order value, item, claim type, and refund deadline
Unboxing photo strip and weight-scan timeline
Policy test cards for honest-customer protection vs abuse prevention
Approve, partial, deny, or escalate decision rail
Customer reply composer that stays firm without sounding accusatory
Weekly fraud pattern wall with repeat items, ZIPs, and claim reasons
phaseA.spreadTrigger: The case-stage view is screenshot-worthy for ops reviews and merchant communities comparing fraud patterns.
phaseA.stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web app prototype called "Return Fraud Inspection Theater" for small ecommerce teams staging suspicious returns, box photos, customer history, and refund rules into a fast approve-deny performance. The first screen must be a working returns case surface with a suspicious return stage, unboxing photo strip, weight-scan timeline, customer history clues, policy test cards, decision rail, customer reply composer, and weekly fraud pattern wall. Use realistic sample data: $289 dress returned after event weekend, package weight mismatch, missing tag photo, repeat buyer with six returns, honest-customer risk note, empty-box claim, and one organized-network warning. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with a memorable stage/backstage composition, bold but readable contrast, one magenta action accent, and recognizable operations controls beneath the concept. Do not make a marketing landing page; the first screen must be the working app.
